title: Global Identification of Principal-Stratum Effects from Three Trials
banked_reason: Cold D0.5 review: sound-and-complete exact-three binary principal-effect atlas, but paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < field threshold 7.4; achieved subfield and no same-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The proved atlas and certificate give a sound-and-complete decision for each named effect on both the target-present and fully positive fibers, including exact unequal-effect witnesses.
This advances beyond the local identification condition in Jiang, Ding, and Geng, but the contribution is confined to binary endpoints and exactly three trials.

The package has exact examples and a transcript construction, yet no worked analysis showing how often the singular certificates change a substantive conclusion; that limits its projected score at a leading econometrics journal.
proof_attempt_summary: The D0 derivation discharged the exact-three binary principal-effect atlas, sound-and-complete certificates for full and positive fibers, and the rank-one boundary transfer theorem; both math and decision panels passed without findings. The D0.5 paper-score gate assigned subfield (6.7 below the field threshold 7.4), with no faithful same-scope repair identified. No Lean formalization was started.
tldr: Can exactly three trials identify a named principal-stratum endpoint effect globally, on fully positive laws, or neither? A complete linked-mixture atlas would answer for every observed law, including singular cancellations and boundary-only failures, with exact compatible counterexample laws.
gap: The direct causal paper supplies a local order condition and numerical examples, not a global named-effect decision across all supports.
fill: Prove separate sound-and-complete two-domain certificates, a target rank-one transfer criterion, and rational witness transcripts.
